stem: In Part B of Assessment 2, how many of the four listed skills will you be assessed on?

options.why: The Canvas page says you will be assessed on two of the listed skills, which will be allocated to you.
You do not choose; skills are allocated, and there are two.
Only two of the four are assessed.

options.text: Three skills, allocated on the day
options.why: The page says two, not three.

explanation: Part B is a 15-minute bedside demonstration of two allocated skills out of: lung auscultation, ECG lead placement, oxygen administration, medication administration via nebuliser. Prepare all four.

stem: Which of these is a 93225 subject topic but NOT one of the four Part B skills?

options.why: Suctioning is a subject topic (Subject Information p.2) but is not on the Part B skills list.
Lung auscultation is one of the four Part B skills.
ECG lead placement is one of the four Part B skills.
Nebuliser medication administration is one of the four Part B skills.

explanation: The Part B list has exactly four skills: lung auscultation, ECG lead placement, oxygen administration, medication administration via nebuliser.

stem: What is the format of Part A of Assessment 2?

options.text: A 15-minute paper-based quiz with multiple-choice and short-answer questions
options.why: The Canvas page describes Part A as a 15-minute paper-based quiz in multiple-choice and short-answer formats.
30 minutes is the total for Parts A and B together; Part A is 15 minutes and paper based.
Part A also includes short-answer questions.

options.text: An oral viva with the assessor
options.why: Part A is a written paper quiz.

explanation: Part A covers all content in your pre-work, lectures and labs so far, so expect both recall and short written reasoning.

stem: Which oxygen delivery devices does the 93225 Subject Information name for managing oxygen therapy?

options.text: Simple face mask (Hudson mask), Venturi mask and non-rebreather mask
options.why: These three devices are named in the content topics and in the core clinical skill.

options.text: Nasal prongs, Hudson mask and Venturi mask only
options.why: The Subject Information names the Hudson, Venturi and non-rebreather masks; nasal prongs are not in that list.

options.text: CPAP, BiPAP and high-flow nasal prongs
options.why: These are not the devices the Subject Information names.
Three devices are named, not one.

explanation: Oxygen therapy with these three devices is also a core clinical skill assessed in the labs (Subject Information p.8). Their flow rates are not in the loaded sources; see Gaps.

stem: How much is Assessment 2 (Parts A and B combined) worth?

options.why: Both the Canvas page and the Subject Information give a weighting of 30%.
20% is Assessment 1 (Medication Calculation Quiz).
50% is Assessment 3 (Case-Based Assessment).
15 is the number of minutes for each part, not the weighting.

explanation: Assessment 2 is individual, worth 30%, and runs in your Week 4 lab (weeks commencing 28 September 2026).
